architecture.approach: Add four single-purpose library crates to the existing Cargo workspace. platform-core owns tenant/provider identity, capabilities, an explicit registry, a token-store contract, secret redaction, and one IntegrationError. quota-ledger reuses platform-core identity types and implements reserve/commit/release over an in-memory store and an optional Postgres backend. hookgate reuses platform-core identity types and implements raw-byte HMAC verification, replay-window checks, durable dedupe, an outbox, and dead-letter replay. syncforge implements a durable action queue, UUID v7 idempotency, per-action batch results, and explicit conflict strategies over Storage and Transport traits. One example inside crates/hookgate/examples composes platform-core, quota-ledger, and hookgate without changing the workspace member glob.

dataModel.flowDescription: platform-core holds no rows. quota-ledger rows are keyed by tenant, provider, metric, and window start, with budget, reservation, and settlement state in Postgres or memory. hookgate rows are delivery records unique on tenant, provider, and event id, plus outbox and dead-letter rows. syncforge rows are actions with payload, client timestamp, idempotency key, status, and attempts. All identifiers are UUIDs and all timestamps are UTC with an explicit client or server source.

securityConsiderations.description: Tenant is part of every store key and every SQL predicate; memory stores key on (TenantId, ProviderId, ...), so no lookup can cross tenants.
Secret and connection strings redact in Debug and Display; secrets do not implement Serialize; errors never include the secret value.
Raw bytes are length-checked, signatures are constant-time compared, timestamps are bounded, and every malformed input returns a typed error.
Parameterized SQL only; fixed table and column names; no caller-supplied identifiers.
One atomic conditional statement per reservation; idempotency enforced by a unique index; settlement is idempotent.
forbid unsafe_code and deny missing_docs in every crate root; rustdoc warnings are denied in verification.
Postgres TLS is required by default; an insecure mode is an explicit test-only opt-in and is documented.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Indexes on (tenant, provider, metric, window_start) and (tenant, provider, event_id) keep lookups logarithmic.
A single conditional UPDATE avoids an application-level read-modify-write round trip.
Ordered in-memory structures, bounded batches, and capped backoff keep replay deterministic and bounded.

risks.description: Four crates in one feature create review fatigue and a long-lived branch.
risks.mitigation: One crate per phase; each phase compiles and documents its public surface independently.

risks.description: Async trait objects break object safety or add hidden allocation costs.
risks.mitigation: async-trait everywhere, object-safe traits, contract suites against memory and mock implementations.

risks.description: No Postgres server is available in every environment or CI.
risks.mitigation: Backend behind a feature; DATABASE_URL opt-in tests; /sdrive:test decides CI provisioning.

risks.description: SQL injection through dynamic SQL or caller identifiers.
risks.mitigation: Fixed schema and parameterized values only; review every query.

risks.description: Timing or replay weaknesses in verification and dedupe.
risks.mitigation: Constant-time comparison, raw bytes, unique constraints, and replay-window checks.

risks.description: Crate names are taken on crates.io.
risks.mitigation: Check immediately before publish; stop on a collision and choose a fallback.

risks.description: New dependencies raise the effective MSRV above 1.85.
risks.mitigation: Existing MSRV CI job; pin or downgrade with a recorded decision.

risks.description: The trait surface becomes too abstract or absorbs product nouns.
risks.mitigation: Review every public type against the catalogue non-goals and the out-of-scope list.
UUID v7 keys, per-action results, deterministic mock tests, and a documented at-least-once contract.

risks.description: Scope creep from deferred features (Redis, SQLite, HTTP, axum, SendGrid).
risks.mitigation: Deferred items are explicit; additions require a new version.
